text: Learning begins with a question. A small experiment makes the question concrete. We write down what we expected, run the experiment, and compare the result with the expectation.
A language model predicts the next token from the tokens before it. During training, the correct next token is already known. The model adjusts its parameters to make observed sequences more likely.

A matrix is a rectangular collection of numbers. Matrix multiplication combines rows and columns through dot products. Shapes tell us which products are defined, but they do not describe how memory is arranged.
A validation document is kept outside the training split. It helps us check whether a model improves on text it has not directly optimized. A useful report states how the split was constructed.
A gradient tells us how a small parameter change affects a local objective. It is not a promise that a large step will improve the objective. The learning rate controls how far we move.
The optimizer stores more than the model parameters. Momentum and adaptive statistics summarize earlier gradients. Continuing training without these states changes the trajectory of the experiment.

A checkpoint contains model weights, optimizer states, and progress. For a reproducible continuation, it also saves random number states and the settings that determine data sampling and learning rates.

Data quality starts before training. Empty documents, exact duplicates, and contaminated evaluation examples can change the meaning of a reported result. We inspect the data rather than assuming every record is useful.
An attention row mixes information from visible positions. A causal mask hides future tokens, so the current prediction cannot read the answer that appears later in the sequence.

Softmax converts scores into normalized weights. Subtracting the maximum score gives an equivalent expression with safer exponentials. Floating point arithmetic still introduces small numerical differences.
The first experiment should be small enough to understand. We check shapes, compare a gradient with a finite difference, and overfit a short batch before spending more time on a larger run.

A training curve describes a particular run. It depends on the dataset, batch construction, optimizer, and random states. We save these conditions alongside the curve so that the observation can be checked.

More parameters do not automatically create a better model. Data, optimization, architecture, and compute interact. We compare alternatives under a clearly stated budget and an independent evaluation.
A tokenizer defines the units predicted by a language model. A byte tokenizer is simple and can represent UTF-8 text. A learned subword tokenizer usually expresses common fragments with fewer tokens.

A residual connection adds a transformed representation to its input. This provides a direct path through a block. Normalization and activation functions determine how that block processes its values.

A useful engineering note includes the question, assumptions, method, and observation. It also records what remains uncertain. A surprising result is a reason to inspect the system, not to hide the measurement.
Padding makes examples fit into rectangular batches. Padded targets are excluded from the loss. When examples have different lengths, their valid token counts matter for averaging the objective.

Gradient accumulation combines several small batches before an optimizer update. Matching a larger batch requires the same objective normalization. Averaging unequal microbatch means can assign the wrong weights.

A GPU runs many pieces of work in parallel. That parallelism is useful only when the workload and data movement allow it. Small operations may be limited by fixed overhead rather than arithmetic throughput.

Temperature changes the distribution used for sampling. A lower temperature concentrates probability, while a higher value spreads it. Sampling settings affect generated text but do not change the trained weights.

Perplexity is the exponential of average negative log likelihood. It must be interpreted with the tokenizer, dataset, and masking rule. Numbers from different tokenizations are not directly comparable.

A document boundary is a useful signal. A beginning marker starts an example and an end marker identifies its completion. Concatenating documents without a boundary can create relationships that were not in the source.
Reproducibility has a scope. An exact continuation on one CPU environment does not prove identical results on every GPU or library version. The report should describe where the check was performed.

A small model trained on a small corpus is an educational experiment. It can demonstrate optimization and generation. It does not establish the knowledge, reasoning, or instruction following of a large deployed system.
When a measurement disagrees with our hypothesis, we first check the measurement boundary. Warmup, synchronization, allocation, and caches can all affect the interpretation of a timing result.

A model can memorize a collection of training examples. Lower training loss alone is therefore not enough. We examine held-out loss and representative failure cases before drawing broader conclusions.
An experiment should change one important factor at a time. If the dataset, batch size, architecture, and schedule all change, it becomes difficult to attribute the outcome to a specific choice.

A production training system must recover from failures. It tracks dataset versions, checkpoints, resources, and validation results. Reliable operations are part of the training method, not an afterthought.

A larger effective batch can reduce the variation of an estimated gradient. It also changes the number of updates for a fixed token budget. Learning rate and schedule choices must account for the experimental goal.

Numerical checks connect equations with code. We perturb one input, measure the output difference, and compare it with the derivative. This helps isolate an indexing mistake from an optimization issue.

An evaluation set should remain independent of model selection. Repeatedly choosing parameters from the same validation set can adapt the experiment to that set. A separate final test answers a different question.
公开的技术报告能够帮助理解训练方法，但没有披露的参数、数据比例和成本不能凭模型表现猜出来。学习时要把可核实的事实与自己的推导分开。
